title: The Boy in the Basement
logline: A man who looks like a kidnapper turns out to be a father taking his son home; the viewer should feel dread for forty seconds and then relief in one word.

beat_feelings.mission: Someone is being hunted and nobody inside knows.
beat_feelings.preparation: He is careful and he has done this before. Nobody can call for help now.
beat_feelings.target: The boy is alone and the man is already in the room.
beat_feelings.strike: This is the worst moment: he takes the child.
beat_feelings.reversal: Wait, the police are his. He is not the danger. He is the boy's father.

look.palette_note: Deep indigo night with moon-blue edges. Warm amber exists only where the story puts safety or life: the lit window at the start, the gap under the kidnappers' door, the dawn-warm light on the last close-up. The boy's pale blue pyjamas are the lightest thing in every frame he is in.
look.light_story: Warm window in a cold night (a home that is not a home) -> the windows go dark and only the moon is left -> the basement is one cold pool of moonlight -> blue and red police light arrives and reads as threat for one second -> a warm soft key opens on the two faces for 'Papa'.

must_not_show.how: seen from behind, as a hand, or as a dark shape against the moonlight

cast.role: the father; reads as an intruder until the last shot
cast.notes: Dark hoodie and trousers as shipped: he should almost disappear into the night. Brows go to 'concerned' in sh05.

cast.role: the son, held in the basement
cast.notes: Pale blue-grey pyjamas as shipped: the brightest costume, so the eye finds him in the dark basement.

sets.description: A lonely two-window house in a clearing, seen from the tree line. Fence, a few bare and pine trees, low hills behind.
sets.key_from: moon high behind the house, screen-right, so the man is a rim-lit shape from behind
practicals: two warm lit windows that switch off during sh01
dressing: phone wire and junction box on the wall by the corner

sets.description: Bare concrete basement: one small high window, a mattress on the floor, a crate, pipes along the wall.
sets.key_from: moon through the high window, a hard cold pool on the floor that the boy lies in
dressing: a school bag in the corner, half in shadow (a fair background clue for the last line)

sets.description: A hallway wall with one closed bedroom door, seen close.
sets.key_from: cool spill from the stairwell, screen-left
practicals: warm line of light under the door: the men are inside

sets.description: Open dark field running down to a road where two police cars wait.
sets.key_from: moon behind-left; police lights from the road, in front of the runners
practicals: alternating blue and red light bars

assets.source_hint: library, else BlenderKit 'wire cutters pliers', else build
library, else build (two cylinders and a bit)

assets.what: chunky clay police car with a light bar
assets.source_hint: library, else BlenderKit 'police car low poly' restyled, else build

shots.vo_text: For three nights, a tall man watched a lonely house from the trees. Tonight, he would take the boy inside. He knew when the lights went out. He knew when the dogs slept.
shots.purpose: Hook: put the viewer behind a watcher. They must feel the house is being studied by someone patient, and that the people inside do not know.
shots.staging: The man stands still at the tree line with his back to us. Far beyond him the house has two warm windows. On 'the lights went out' the windows go dark one after the other. He does not move until the narrator has finished, then takes one step forward.

camera.start: Over his right shoulder, low and close: his dark back fills the left third, the house is small and sharp in the upper-middle. 40 mm.

moves.at: from the first word to 'the boy inside'
moves.move: very slow dolly forward past his shoulder
moves.why: We lean in with him: the watching becomes a decision.

moves.at: 'He knew when the lights went out'
moves.why: The light change is the event; a moving camera would compete with it.

focus.why: The narrator is talking about what he watches, so the house is sharp and he is a soft dark shape.
The sentence turns from the house to his intention; attention moves to him without a cut.

focus.at: 'He knew when the lights went out'
focus.why: So the viewer watches the windows die.

light_change.what: the two windows switch off, left then right, 0.7 s apart
light_change.why: It is literally what the narrator says, and it removes the only warm thing in the frame.

shots.sound: night insects, far wind; a soft switch click with each window; music is one low held note

shots.vo_text: In the dark, he cut the phone line.
shots.why_cut: A jump in scale from the whole house to one wire: the clue must be the only thing in the frame, and a move from the tree line to the wall would take ten seconds.
shots.purpose: Clue one and the point of no return. The viewer must read 'the phone line is cut' in under a second, and feel that nobody can call for help.
shots.staging: Close on the house wall: a black wire runs down to a small junction box. A hand holding cutters comes in from screen-left and the jaws reach the wire on the word 'cut'. The lower half of the wire swings away.

camera.start: Insert, 85 mm, from his right side along the wall: wire in the middle of frame, wall filling the background. Only his hand and the tool ever enter.

moves.why: The frame tightens as the cutters close; then it is still for the fall.

focus.on: the wire at the point of the cut
focus.why: Nothing else exists in this shot.

shots.sound: one dry metal snip exactly on 'cut', then the loose wire tapping the wall; music drops out for the snip

shots.vo_text: At midnight, he climbed through a window. Two men slept upstairs. In the basement, a small boy lay alone. He crossed the room without a sound. He put his hand over the boy's mouth and lifted him.
shots.why_cut: New place and a jump in time ('At midnight'): we are inside now.
shots.purpose: The target and the strike in one unbroken take, so the dread has no exit: first the boy alone in a pool of moonlight, then the dark shape arriving behind him, then the reach.
shots.staging: The boy lies on a mattress in a pool of moonlight, eyes open, looking at the ceiling. The man is already inside, out of frame by the window wall (the climb is not shown: 'he climbed through a window' plays on the window itself). On 'He crossed the room' he walks slowly behind the mattress, his head above the frame line. On 'put his hand' he crouches just outside frame-left and one hand reaches in toward the boy's face; the boy's brows jump to shocked and his head tips back toward the hand. The lift is not shown: the shot ends on the reach.

camera.start: High small window, moon-blue, top of frame; 35 mm, camera low near the floor.

moves.at: 'Two men slept upstairs. In the basement'
moves.move: crane down and tilt from the window to the boy on the mattress
moves.why: The narrator moves from upstairs to the basement, and the camera makes the same move: down, to the one who is alone.

moves.at: 'He crossed the room' to the end
moves.move: slow dolly in toward the boy's face while the shape crosses behind and the hand enters
moves.why: The room gets smaller around the boy as the threat closes; the viewer cannot back away.

focus.why: It is the way in; the narrator is talking about it.
Empathy: this is who we fear for.

focus.on: stays on the boy; the man is a soft shape behind and above the frame line
focus.why: A shape growing behind a sharp, unaware face is the scariest version, and it keeps the man's face hidden fairly.

clues: put his hand over the boy's mouth
shots.sound: room tone, a pipe ticking; no footsteps at all ('without a sound'); one sharp breath in on the reach; low strings rise under the last sentence

shots.vo_text: On the way out, he locked the two men inside their room.
shots.why_cut: New place, and the third clue needs its own clean frame. It also covers the lift, which is not shown.
shots.purpose: Clue three. It reads as cruelty now (he traps them) and as care after the flip (he holds them for the police). The viewer must see: a door, a key turning, light inside.
shots.staging: A closed door with a warm line of light under it. The key in the lock turns a quarter turn on 'locked', on its own: its bow goes from upright to flat. He has been standing just out of frame; after the turn he walks away.

camera.start: Close on the knob, lock plate and key, 70 mm, slightly from the right so the key's bow reads.

moves.move: pull back and tilt down until the warm gap under the door is in frame
moves.why: Leaving: the men are shut in with their light, and he is already walking away.

focus.why: The object acts; fingers would be hard to animate well and add nothing.

clues: locked the two men inside their room
shots.sound: a heavy lock clunk on 'locked'; faint snoring behind the door

shots.vo_text: He ran across the dark field with the boy in his arms. Police cars waited at the road. He had called them. Five days ago, those men took the boy from school. The boy held him tight and whispered, "Papa."
shots.why_cut: Outside, the escape. The last shot carries the whole reversal in one take so the meaning flips in front of the viewer instead of between cuts.
shots.purpose: The reversal. For one sentence the police lights look like he is caught; then 'He had called them' flips it. End on the first clear look at his face, next to the boy's, in warm light.
shots.staging: Two police cars wait at the road; we look over the light bar of the nearer one. Far across the field the man hurries toward us carrying the boy in both arms. Blue and red light starts as the narrator names the police cars and washes over the pair as they come closer. He stops in front of the car. On 'The boy held him tight' the boy looks up at him; the man's brows soften from stern to concerned and he looks down at the boy.

camera.start: Wide, 35 mm, from behind the waiting police car: its light bar soft and bright in the lower foreground, two small figures far away in a big moonlit field.

moves.move: hold, let them come to us
moves.why: Distance and darkness make them fragile; the approach is the action.

moves.move: rise over the car and push in to the two faces, ending in a close two-shot
moves.why: The truth arrives as we finally get close enough to see who he is.
The last word needs silence in the picture too.

focus.why: They are small; they must be the sharpest thing.

focus.on: the boy's face, the man's just behind the focus plane
focus.why: The last word is the boy's.

light_change.what: police blue/red starts as they come into range; on 'Five days ago' a warm soft key fades up from the cars' side
light_change.why: Threat colour first, then safety: the light tells the flip one beat after the words.

shots.sound: running feet in grass, breath; police radio murmur; everything thins out before 'Papa', which is nearly dry; one warm chord after it

sound.delivery: Low and measured for four beats, no drama in the voice: the words are frightening enough. A breath before 'He had called them'. The last sentence is slower and warmer; 'Papa' is close and quiet.
sound.music: Dark minimal underscore: one low sustained string note and soft felt-piano pulses, no drums, 60 bpm. It thins to almost nothing under the last line and resolves to one warm major chord after 'Papa'.
sound.ambience: night exterior (insects, light wind) for house and field; dead room tone with a ticking pipe for the basement
